title: pressing ESC clear the contents of multiselect
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Pressing ESC (once or twice) clears the contents of a multiselect.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

msg = "What are your favorite colors?"
colors = ["Green", "Yellow", "Red", "Blue"]

options = st.multiselect(msg, colors, default=colors, key="1")
st.write("You selected:", options)

with st.popover("Popover"):
    options = st.multiselect(msg, colors, default=colors, key="2")
    st.write("You selected:", options)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click on the first multiselect to open it
2. Press ESC twice (the options are cleared)
3. Open the popover to see the second multiselect
4. Press ESC to close the popover (the options are cleared)

### Expected Behavior

If you press ESC (no matter how many times) when a multiselect has focus, the options remain the same.

### Current Behavior

Pressing ESC (once or twice) clears the contents of a multiselect.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Opera, Edge, Firefox, Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

I see that for `st.selectbox` if the user provides a default, we make the widget not clearable. Perhaps `st.multiselect` should be made consistent with that? cc [USER]

> I see that for st.selectbox if the user provides a default, we make the widget not clearable. Perhaps st.multiselect should be made consistent with that?

Hm, I think I'd avoid such a behavior change because it could break certain apps in the sense that they rely on clearing all items. Plus, it's a bit arbitrary that if e.g. you set 3 items as default, you can clear two of them, but then you can't clear the last one. 


Also FYI that [USER] is currently porting these components to react-aria, so it probably makes sense to wait with any changes until that's done, so we can see what the supported behaviors in react-aria are.
